However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not organically comparable** to the others: Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and consolidated Hawaiian's results only from that date forward, adding $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss to the period [DOC-2]. Alaska's full-year figures therefore reflect a partial-period, acquisition-inflated revenue base and an acquisition-depressed profit. Also note Southwest's net income ($465M) exceeds its operating income ($321M), indicating profit supported by non-operating items rather than core operations [DOC-1].

**Absolute profitability (FY2024):**

| Airline | Operating income | Net income | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $5,995M [DOC-1] | $3,457M [DOC-1] | 5.6% |
| United | $5,096M [DOC-1] | $3,149M [DOC-1] | 5.5% |
| American | $2,614M [DOC-1] | $846M [DOC-1] | 1.6% |
| Alaska | $570M [DOC-1] | $395M [DOC-1] | 3.4% |
| Southwest | $321M [DOC-1] | $465M [DOC-1] | 1.7% |

**Conclusion:** Delta Air Lines was the most profitable on every measure — the largest operating income ($5,995M vs. United's $5,096M), the largest net income ($3,457M vs. United's $3,149M), and the highest net margin (~5.6%) [DOC-1]. United is a close second; the ranking between them is not affected by the Alaska/Hawaiian comparability issue, since Delta leads by roughly $900M of operating income and $308M of net income.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — highest FY2024 operating income ($5,995M), net income ($3,457M), and net margin (~5.6%), ahead of United ($5,096M / $3,149M); note Alaska's FY2024 is not organically comparable because it includes Hawaiian only from September 18, 2024.
